content.value_statement: Agent systems are hard to test because valid behavior can vary across runs. This skill provides rubrics, metrics, and workflows for repeatable evaluation.
actual_capabilities: Defines evaluation dimensions for factual accuracy, completeness, citation accuracy, source quality, and tool efficiency.
Explains how to create weighted rubrics with clear scoring levels.
Guides test set design across simple, medium, complex, and extended tasks.
Supports evaluation of context engineering choices and degradation behavior.
Provides sample Python evaluator scripts for scoring and summarizing results.
Recommends continuous evaluation pipelines and production monitoring practices.
limitations: The sample evaluator uses simple heuristics and needs customization for production use.
It does not include a hosted dashboard or managed evaluation service.
Human review is still needed for subtle quality, bias, and safety issues.
Metrics must be adapted to each agent domain and risk tolerance.

use_cases.title: Release Quality Gates
use_cases.description: Evaluate agent changes before release using pass thresholds and weighted quality dimensions.

use_cases.title: Context Strategy Comparison
use_cases.description: Compare prompts, tools, memory, and context windows with consistent tests and metrics.

use_cases.title: Production Quality Monitoring
use_cases.description: Sample live interactions and track score trends to detect regressions early.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Rubric
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for one agent workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a simple evaluation rubric for my agent. Include factual accuracy, completeness, and tool efficiency with clear pass criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Test Set
prompt_templates.scenario: Build coverage across task complexity levels.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a test set for this agent workflow. Include simple, medium, complex, and long-running tasks with expected outcomes.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Agent Versions
prompt_templates.scenario: Measure whether a change improved quality.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare two agent configurations using a weighted rubric. Report score changes, regressions, and likely causes.

prompt_templates.title: Build Continuous Evaluation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a continuous evaluation plan for production agents. Include sampling, LLM-as-judge review, human review, alerts, and trend reporting.

output_examples.input: Evaluate a research agent that answers factual questions with citations.
output_examples.output: A rubric with weighted scores for factual accuracy, citation accuracy, source quality, completeness, and tool efficiency.

output_examples.input: Check whether a new context strategy improved agent performance.
output_examples.output: A comparison plan with shared test cases, baseline scores, changed scores, and regression notes.

output_examples.input: Create production monitoring for an agent support workflow.
output_examples.output: A monitoring approach with sampled conversations, recurring evaluation, alert thresholds, and human review checkpoints.

best_practices: Evaluate outcomes and process quality instead of requiring one exact execution path.
Use representative test sets that include normal tasks, edge cases, and long interactions.
Combine automated judging with human review for important or ambiguous cases.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on one aggregate score without checking individual dimensions.
Do not evaluate only easy examples that hide regressions in complex tasks.
Do not treat LLM judge results as final without calibration or spot checks.

faq.question: What does this skill evaluate?
faq.answer: It evaluates agent outputs, tool use, citation behavior, source quality, completeness, and performance over time.

faq.question: Can it replace human review?
faq.answer: No. It helps scale review, but humans should inspect edge cases, safety issues, and high-impact decisions.

faq.question: Does it support LLM-as-judge workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how to structure judge prompts, dimensions, scoring levels, and review outputs.

faq.question: Can I compare two agent versions?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the same test set and rubric to compare score changes, regressions, and efficiency differences.

faq.question: Does it include runnable code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes Python evaluator examples that demonstrate scoring, history tracking, and summaries.

faq.question: What should I customize first?
faq.answer: Start with evaluation dimensions, weights, pass thresholds, and test cases that match your real user tasks.
